build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: The player lays rail tracks between cities on a terrain map by clicking. Track cost varies by terrain crossed (plains cheap, mountains expensive, rivers require bridges). A money counter decreases with each track segment placed. Score 0 if there is no track-laying mechanic, if terrain has no cost effect, or if tracks are free.

Trains are purchased and assigned to routes between connected cities. Trains move automatically along tracks, picking up cargo at one city and delivering to another. Revenue is generated on delivery. Score 0 if trains cannot be bought, if they do not move along tracks, or if delivery generates no revenue.

Cities have cargo demand: each city produces specific goods and consumes others. Delivering goods a city needs pays well; delivering unwanted goods pays poorly. Demand is visible on the map. Score 0 if all deliveries pay equally, if cities have no demand system, or if cargo type does not matter.

A money economy drives the game: track costs and train purchases are upfront expenses, revenue trickles from deliveries. A money counter is permanently visible. Going bankrupt ends the game. Score 0 if there is no money system or if the player cannot go bankrupt.

The full loop connects: title -> new map -> build tracks/buy trains/manage routes -> time advances -> game ends after set years -> result screen with net worth ranking. Score 0 if any transition is missing or if there is no end condition.
At least four terrain types exist (plains, hills, mountains, rivers) with different visual appearances and track-building costs. Score 0 if terrain is uniform or if fewer than three types exist.

At least four cargo types exist (lumber, grain, ore, manufactured goods) with different city production/consumption patterns. Score 0 if only one cargo type exists or if all cities produce the same thing.
At least two train types exist with different speeds, capacities, and costs. Upgrading to faster trains improves route profitability. Score 0 if only one train type exists or if types are identical.

A competitor AI builds its own rail network and competes for cargo demand. If the competitor connects a route first, demand is split or reduced. Score 0 if there is no competitor or if the AI never builds.

At least six cities exist on the map with different goods profiles, creating a network of potential routes. The map is large enough for meaningful routing decisions. Score 0 if fewer than four cities exist or if all cities are identical.
The HUD shows money, year/time, active trains, and revenue summary in clear non-overlapping regions. City demand is readable on the map. Score 0 if money, time, or demand info is missing.

The map clearly shows terrain types, cities with goods icons, laid tracks, and moving trains. Player and competitor tracks are distinguishable. Score 0 if terrain is uniform, if cities are unlabeled, or if tracks are invisible.

Actions produce visible feedback: laying track shows it appear on the map, trains move visibly along routes, deliveries show revenue popups, and track cost is shown before confirming. Score 0 if actions produce no observable change.

Overall art coherence: terrain, cities, tracks, trains, UI, and effects belong to a consistent industrial-era railroad visual language with warm earthy tones. Score 0 if the screen mixes incompatible styles or reads as plain default plain grey. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.
Train sprites are real illustrated or pixel-art locomotives with visible wheels and cargo cars. Different train types have distinct appearances. Score 0 if trains are plain colored shapes.
The terrain map uses real textured tiles (green plains, brown hills, grey mountains, blue rivers) with city illustrations showing buildings and industry. Score 0 if the map is flat colored regions.

HUD and UI use styled themed widgets with industrial-era chrome: money display has coin styling, route panels have ledger aesthetics, and menus have brass-and-wood backgrounds. Score 0 if UI elements are unstyled HTML 引擎 defaults.

Animation and atmosphere: trains move with steam effects, track laying shows construction, cities show activity (smoke, movement), and the map has ambient life (weather, day/night). Score 0 if all elements are static.
